fixes.explanation: Power isn't what Solomon names here. He says, “A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.” Notice what he sets against wealth. It's honor, something a bank account can't hand you. The ruthless men pile up money, and the gracious woman ends up with a good name.

Wandering is a fair guess, but the verse doesn't say it. Solomon says, “Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.” The first half is a warning, and the second half is a way out. Escape is the opposite of being caught in that punishment, so there's no wandering around lost in it.

I wish that worked, but the verse says the opposite. Solomon says, “He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.” Think of the two pictures. One man is leaning his whole weight on his money, and down he goes. The righteous are leafy and green, still growing.

Rich is a fair guess, but the verse doesn't say it. Solomon says, “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.” He sets a tree of life next to winning souls, and the reward he names is wisdom. Wisdom is the kind of treasure that bears fruit for other people, not just for your own pocket.
